reasons.A: Modern first-person, confessional and hedged ('I think', 'Perhaps'), plain contemporary diction and even sentences; nothing of the passage's lofty third-person stance or dashes and semicolons.
reasons.B: Period register and third-person 'the grown man' fit, with dashes and balanced antitheses, but it slides into an arguing 'we' and a reproachful ending the passage never adopts.
reasons.C: Closest movement: impersonal 'the child'/'grown man', short assertive sentences set against long cadenced ones, 'not X but Y' refinements joined by semicolons and dashes, and aphoristic abstraction ('habit has abolished it') like the passage's.
